"""plant_canaries.py -- Phase 8, part 2.

Injects marker phrases into a built tree from a manifest CSV. Originals are
backed up first and every file's original timestamps are restored afterwards,
so planting leaves no trace in the mtime distribution.

Usage
-----
    python plant_canaries.py --manifest slots.csv [--corpus ..\corpus_15000]
                             [--backup ..\keys\plant_backups] [--dry-run]
    python plant_canaries.py --restore --backup ..\keys\plant_backups

Manifest columns
----------------
    phrase   the string to inject (required)
    path     corpus-relative path of the target file (required)
    page     for a PDF, the 0-based page index to inject on (optional; default 0)
    where    optional hint: `end` (default), `start`, or a line number for text

Supported targets: .md .txt .csv .json .do .R .log (text insertion), .pdf
(a text object added to the named page), .docx (a paragraph), .xlsx (a cell),
.zip (a member file is rewritten and the archive rebuilt).

A scanned PDF has no text layer; injecting text into one is refused with a
clear message, because the useful thing there is that it cannot be found.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
DEFAULT_CORPUS = ROOT / "corpus_15000"
DEFAULT_BACKUP = ROOT / "keys" / "plant_backups"
TEXTY = {".md", ".txt", ".csv", ".json", ".do", ".r", ".log", ".tex", ".py"}


def times_of(p: Path):
    st = p.stat()
    return (st.st_atime, st.st_mtime)


def restore_times(p: Path, t):
    os.utime(p, t)


def backup(p: Path, corpus: Path, backup_dir: Path) -> Path:
    rel = p.relative_to(corpus)
    dst = backup_dir / rel
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not dst.exists():
        shutil.copy2(p, dst)
    return dst


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def plant_text(p: Path, phrase: str, where: str) -> bool:
    raw = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    line = phrase if raw.endswith("\n") or not raw else f"\n{phrase}"
    if p.suffix.lower() == ".json":
        try:
            obj = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            p.write_text(raw.rstrip() + f"\n{phrase}\n", encoding="utf-8")
            return True
        if isinstance(obj, dict):
            obj["note"] = phrase
        elif isinstance(obj, list):
            obj.append({"note": phrase})
        p.write_text(json.dumps(obj, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
        return True
    if where == "start":
        p.write_text(f"{phrase}\n{raw}", encoding="utf-8")
    elif where.isdigit():
        lines = raw.splitlines(keepends=True)
        i = min(int(where), len(lines))
        lines.insert(i, phrase + "\n")
        p.write_text("".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
    else:
        p.write_text(raw.rstrip("\n") + line + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return True


def plant_pdf(p: Path, phrase: str, page: int) -> bool:
    import io
    from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter
    from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas as rl_canvas

    reader = PdfReader(str(p))
    n = len(reader.pages)
    if page < 0 or page >= n:
        print(f"  ! page {page} out of range (document has {n}); using the last page")
        page = n - 1
    target = reader.pages[page]
    if not (target.extract_text() or "").strip():
        print(f"  ! {p.name} page {page} has no text layer -- refusing to inject text "
              f"into a scan. Leave this slot as a negative control.")
        return False
    w = float(target.mediabox.width)
    h = float(target.mediabox.height)
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    c = rl_canvas.Canvas(buf, pagesize=(w, h))
    c.setFont("Helvetica", 7)
    c.drawString(36, 24, phrase)
    c.save()
    buf.seek(0)
    overlay = PdfReader(buf).pages[0]
    writer = PdfWriter()
    for i, pg in enumerate(reader.pages):
        if i == page:
            pg.merge_page(overlay)
        writer.add_page(pg)
    tmp = p.with_suffix(p.suffix + ".tmp")
    with tmp.open("wb") as fh:
        writer.write(fh)
    tmp.replace(p)
    return True


def plant_docx(p: Path, phrase: str) -> bool:
    import docx
    d = docx.Document(str(p))
    d.add_paragraph(phrase)
    d.save(str(p))
    return True


def plant_xlsx(p: Path, phrase: str) -> bool:
    import openpyxl
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(str(p))
    ws = wb[wb.sheetnames[0]]
    ws.cell(row=ws.max_row + 2, column=1, value=phrase)
    wb.save(str(p))
    return True


def plant_zip(p: Path, phrase: str, member: str | None) -> bool:
    tmp = p.with_suffix(".tmp.zip")
    with zipfile.ZipFile(p, "r") as zin:
        names = zin.namelist()
        target = member
        if target is None:
            texty = [n for n in names if Path(n).suffix.lower() in TEXTY]
            target = texty[0] if texty else (names[0] if names else None)
        if target is None:
            print(f"  ! {p.name} is empty")
            return False
        with zipfile.ZipFile(tmp, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zout:
            for info in zin.infolist():
                data = zin.read(info.filename)
                if info.filename == target:
                    if Path(target).suffix.lower() in TEXTY:
                        data = data.rstrip(b"\n") + b"\n" + phrase.encode("utf-8") + b"\n"
                    else:
                        print(f"  ! member {target} is not a text file; appending a sibling")
                        zout.writestr(info, data)
                        zout.writestr(str(Path(target).with_suffix(".note.txt")), phrase)
                        continue
                zout.writestr(info, data)
    tmp.replace(p)
    return True


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def plant_one(corpus: Path, backup_dir: Path, row: dict, dry: bool) -> str:
    rel = row["path"].strip().replace("\\", "/")
    phrase = row["phrase"]
    page = int(row.get("page") or 0)
    where = (row.get("where") or "end").strip()
    p = corpus / rel
    if not p.exists():
        return f"MISSING  {rel}"
    if dry:
        return f"would plant into {rel} (page {page})"
    t = times_of(p)
    backup(p, corpus, backup_dir)
    ext = p.suffix.lower()
    try:
        if ext == ".pdf":
            ok = plant_pdf(p, phrase, page)
        elif ext == ".docx":
            ok = plant_docx(p, phrase)
        elif ext == ".xlsx":
            ok = plant_xlsx(p, phrase)
        elif ext == ".zip":
            ok = plant_zip(p, phrase, row.get("member") or None)
        elif ext in TEXTY:
            ok = plant_text(p, phrase, where)
        else:
            return f"UNSUPPORTED  {rel} ({ext})"
    except Exception as exc:
        return f"FAILED  {rel}: {exc}"
    finally:
        if p.exists():
            restore_times(p, t)
    return ("planted  " if ok else "skipped  ") + rel


def restore_all(corpus: Path, backup_dir: Path) -> int:
    n = 0
    for src in backup_dir.rglob("*"):
        if not src.is_file():
            continue
        rel = src.relative_to(backup_dir)
        dst = corpus / rel
        t = times_of(src)
        dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(src, dst)
        restore_times(dst, t)
        n += 1
    return n


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--manifest")

"""plant_canaries.py -- Phase 8, part 2.

Injects marker phrases into a built tree from a manifest CSV. Originals are
backed up first and every file's original timestamps are restored afterwards,
so planting leaves no trace in the mtime distribution.

Usage
-----
    python plant_canaries.py --manifest slots.csv [--corpus ..\corpus_15000]
                             [--backup ..\keys\plant_backups] [--dry-run]
    python plant_canaries.py --restore --backup ..\keys\plant_backups

Manifest columns
----------------
    phrase   the string to inject (required)
    path     corpus-relative path of the target file (required)
    page     for a PDF, the 0-based page index to inject on (optional; default 0)
    where    optional hint: `end` (default), `start`, or a line number for text

Supported targets: .md .txt .csv .json .do .R .log (text insertion), .pdf
(a text object added to the named page), .docx (a paragraph), .xlsx (a cell),
.zip (a member file is rewritten and the archive rebuilt).

A scanned PDF has no text layer; injecting text into one is refused with a
clear message, because the useful thing there is that it cannot be found.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
DEFAULT_CORPUS = ROOT / "corpus_15000"
DEFAULT_BACKUP = ROOT / "keys" / "plant_backups"
TEXTY = {".md", ".txt", ".csv", ".json", ".do", ".r", ".log", ".tex", ".py"}


def times_of(p: Path):
    st = p.stat()
    return (st.st_atime, st.st_mtime)


def restore_times(p: Path, t):
    os.utime(p, t)


def backup(p: Path, corpus: Path, backup_dir: Path) -> Path:
    rel = p.relative_to(corpus)
    dst = backup_dir / rel
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if not dst.exists():
        shutil.copy2(p, dst)
    return dst


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def plant_text(p: Path, phrase: str, where: str) -> bool:
    raw = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    line = phrase if raw.endswith("\n") or not raw else f"\n{phrase}"
    if p.suffix.lower() == ".json":
        try:
            obj = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            p.write_text(raw.rstrip() + f"\n{phrase}\n", encoding="utf-8")
            return True
        if isinstance(obj, dict):
            obj["note"] = phrase
        elif isinstance(obj, list):
            obj.append({"note": phrase})
        p.write_text(json.dumps(obj, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
        return True
    if where == "start":
        p.write_text(f"{phrase}\n{raw}", encoding="utf-8")
    elif where.isdigit():
        lines = raw.splitlines(keepends=True)
        i = min(int(where), len(lines))
        lines.insert(i, phrase + "\n")
        p.write_text("".join(lines), encoding="utf-8")
    else:
        p.write_text(raw.rstrip("\n") + line + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return True


def plant_pdf(p: Path, phrase: str, page: int) -> bool:
    import io
    from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter
    from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas as rl_canvas

    reader = PdfReader(str(p))
    n = len(reader.pages)
    if page < 0 or page >= n:
        print(f"  ! page {page} out of range (document has {n}); using the last page")
        page = n - 1
    target = reader.pages[page]
    if not (target.extract_text() or "").strip():
        print(f"  ! {p.name} page {page} has no text layer -- refusing to inject text "
              f"into a scan. Leave this slot as a negative control.")
        return False
    w = float(target.mediabox.width)
    h = float(target.mediabox.height)
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    c = rl_canvas.Canvas(buf, pagesize=(w, h))
    c.setFont("Helvetica", 7)
    c.drawString(36, 24, phrase)
    c.save()
    buf.seek(0)
    overlay = PdfReader(buf).pages[0]
    writer = PdfWriter()
    for i, pg in enumerate(reader.pages):
        if i == page:
            pg.merge_page(overlay)
        writer.add_page(pg)
    tmp = p.with_suffix(p.suffix + ".tmp")
    with tmp.open("wb") as fh:
        writer.write(fh)
    tmp.replace(p)
    return True


def plant_docx(p: Path, phrase: str) -> bool:
    import docx
    d = docx.Document(str(p))
    d.add_paragraph(phrase)
    d.save(str(p))
    return True


def plant_xlsx(p: Path, phrase: str) -> bool:
    import openpyxl
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(str(p))
    ws = wb[wb.sheetnames[0]]
    ws.cell(row=ws.max_row + 2, column=1, value=phrase)
    wb.save(str(p))
    return True


def plant_zip(p: Path, phrase: str, member: str | None) -> bool:
    tmp = p.with_suffix(".tmp.zip")
    with zipfile.ZipFile(p, "r") as zin:
        names = zin.namelist()
        target = member
        if target is None:
            texty = [n for n in names if Path(n).suffix.lower() in TEXTY]
            target = texty[0] if texty else (names[0] if names else None)
        if target is None:
            print(f"  ! {p.name} is empty")
            return False
        with zipfile.ZipFile(tmp, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zout:
            for info in zin.infolist():
                data = zin.read(info.filename)
                if info.filename == target:
                    if Path(target).suffix.lower() in TEXTY:
                        data = data.rstrip(b"\n") + b"\n" + phrase.encode("utf-8") + b"\n"
                    else:
                        print(f"  ! member {target} is not a text file; appending a sibling")
                        zout.writestr(info, data)
                        zout.writestr(str(Path(target).with_suffix(".note.txt")), phrase)
                        continue
                zout.writestr(info, data)
    tmp.replace(p)
    return True


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def plant_one(corpus: Path, backup_dir: Path, row: dict, dry: bool) -> str:
    rel = row["path"].strip().replace("\\", "/")
    phrase = row["phrase"]
    page = int(row.get("page") or 0)
    where = (row.get("where") or "end").strip()
    p = corpus / rel
    if not p.exists():
        return f"MISSING  {rel}"
    if dry:
        return f"would plant into {rel} (page {page})"
    t = times_of(p)
    backup(p, corpus, backup_dir)
    ext = p.suffix.lower()
    try:
        if ext == ".pdf":
            ok = plant_pdf(p, phrase, page)
        elif ext == ".docx":
            ok = plant_docx(p, phrase)
        elif ext == ".xlsx":
            ok = plant_xlsx(p, phrase)
        elif ext == ".zip":
            ok = plant_zip(p, phrase, row.get("member") or None)
        elif ext in TEXTY:
            ok = plant_text(p, phrase, where)
        else:
            return f"UNSUPPORTED  {rel} ({ext})"
    except Exception as exc:
        return f"FAILED  {rel}: {exc}"
    finally:
        if p.exists():
            restore_times(p, t)
    return ("planted  " if ok else "skipped  ") + rel


def restore_all(corpus: Path, backup_dir: Path) -> int:
    n = 0
    for src in backup_dir.rglob("*"):
        if not src.is_file():
            continue
        rel = src.relative_to(backup_dir)
        dst = corpus / rel
        t = times_of(src)
        dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(src, dst)
        restore_times(dst, t)
        n += 1
    return n


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--manifest")
    ap.add_argument("--corpus", default=str(DEFAULT_CORPUS))
    ap.add_argument("--backup", default=str(DEFAULT_BACKUP))
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--restore", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    corpus, backup_dir = Path(a.corpus), Path(a.backup)

    if a.restore:
        n = restore_all(corpus, backup_dir)
        print(f"restored {n} files from {backup_dir}")
        return
    if not a.manifest:
        ap.error("--manifest is required unless --restore is given")
    backup_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(a.manifest, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    print(f"{len(rows)} rows, corpus {corpus}")
    results = [plant_one(corpus, backup_dir, r, a.dry_run) for r in rows]
    for r in results:
        print("  " + r)
    ok = sum(1 for r in results if r.startswith("planted"))
    print(f"\n{ok}/{len(rows)} planted. Backups in {backup_dir}. "
          f"Undo with: python plant_canaries.py --restore --backup {backup_dir}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""finalize_key.py -- resolve logical evidence addresses to physical ones.

Phase 3 recorded where every piece of evidence went, logically: which document,
which chapter, which table, which series vintage, which fiscal year. It could
not record the page index, because that depends on how the document laid out.

This step fills that in from the sidecars the PDF factory wrote for its own
output, and hashes every file. It does not search the corpus: for each address
it goes straight to the one file the key already names.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
CFG = yaml.safe_load((HERE / "config.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
KEYS = ROOT / "keys"
TOP = CFG["ladder"][-1]
CORPUS = ROOT / f"corpus_{TOP}"
INDEX = KEYS / "pdf_index"


def sha256(p: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with p.open("rb") as fh:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def sidecar(rel: str):
    p = INDEX / (hashlib.sha256(rel.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:32] + ".json")
    if p.exists():
        try:
            return json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            return None
    return None


def match_table(sc, ev):
    if not sc or not sc.get("tables"):
        return None
    ts = sc["tables"]
    exact = [t for t in ts
             if t.get("series_id") == ev.get("series_id")
             and t.get("vintage_id") == ev.get("vintage_id")
             and (ev.get("chapter") is None or t.get("chapter") == ev.get("chapter"))
             and (ev.get("table_ordinal") is None
                  or t.get("table_ordinal") == ev.get("table_ordinal"))]
    if exact:
        return exact[0]
    same = [t for t in ts if t.get("series_id") == ev.get("series_id")]
    if same:
        return same[0]
    return None


def main():
    key = json.loads((KEYS / "answer_key.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    hashes: dict[str, str] = {}
    stats = {"addresses": 0, "hashed": 0, "resolved_pages": 0,
             "missing_file": [], "no_sidecar": [], "no_table": []}

    def resolve(ev):
        stats["addresses"] += 1
        rel = ev["path"]
        p = CORPUS / rel
        if not p.exists():
            stats["missing_file"].append(rel)
            return
        if rel not in hashes:
            hashes[rel] = sha256(p)
            stats["hashed"] += 1
        ev["content_hash"] = hashes[rel]
        ev["size_bytes"] = p.stat().st_size
        if not rel.lower().endswith(".pdf"):
            return
        sc = sidecar(rel)
        if sc is None:
            stats["no_sidecar"].append(rel)
            return
        ev["n_pages"] = sc.get("n_pages")
        ev["has_text_layer"] = sc.get("has_text_layer", True)
        t = match_table(sc, ev)
        if t is None:
            stats["no_table"].append(rel)
            return
        ev["page_index"] = t.get("page_index")
        ev["page_label"] = t.get("page_label")
        ev["table_title"] = t.get("table_title")
        if ev.get("row") is None:
            ev["row"] = t.get("row_label")
        rows, cols = t.get("rows") or {}, t.get("cols") or {}
        ev["row_position"] = rows.get(ev.get("row") or t.get("row_label"))
        ev["col_position"] = cols.get(ev.get("col") or ev.get("fy"))
        stats["resolved_pages"] += 1

    for q in key["questions"]:
        for ev in q["evidence_addresses"]:
            resolve(ev)
    for lk in key.get("relationship_links", []):
        for ev in lk["evidence"]:
            resolve(ev)

    # hash the shadow copies too, so a scorer can identify them by content
    for path, d in key.get("distractor_files", {}).items():
        p = CORPUS / path
        if p.exists():
            d["content_hash"] = hashes.get(path) or sha256(p)
        else:
            d["content_hash"] = None

    key["finalised"] = {k: (v if not isinstance(v, list) else
                            {"count": len(v), "sample": sorted(set(v))[:10]})
                        for k, v in stats.items()}
    (KEYS / "answer_key.json").write_text(json.dumps(key, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"addresses        : {stats['addresses']}")
    print(f"files hashed     : {stats['hashed']}")
    print(f"page addresses   : {stats['resolved_pages']}")
    print(f"missing files    : {len(stats['missing_file'])}")
    print(f"no sidecar       : {len(stats['no_sidecar'])}")
    print(f"no matching table: {len(stats['no_table'])}")
    for k in ("missing_file", "no_sidecar", "no_table"):
        if stats[k]:
            print(f"  {k} sample: {sorted(set(stats[k]))[:5]}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""determinism.py -- verification check 9.

Regenerates from the same config into a scratch directory and compares.

Two stages:

  1. the planning layer -- the world, the file plan, the key and the rung
     membership. These must be byte-identical.
  2. the content layer -- the files of the 500 rung, rebuilt by the same
     factories into a scratch corpus and compared hash for hash.

The scratch copy is relocated by rewriting the absolute root path inside the
copied scripts, so a factory that hardcodes its paths still runs against the
scratch tree. The authored documents are fixed inputs and are copied across
unchanged, exactly as the brief specifies.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
KEYS = ROOT / "keys"
PY = ROOT / "generator" / ".venv" / "Scripts" / "python.exe"

PLAN_ARTEFACTS = [
    "world/series_registry.json", "world/series_vintages.json", "world/series_breaks.json",
    "world/entities.json", "world/document_catalogue.json",
    "keys/skeleton_manifest.json", "keys/rung_membership.json",
]
# fields written by finalize_key.py, which runs against real bytes and so is
# not part of the planning layer
VOLATILE_KEY_FIELDS = {"content_hash", "size_bytes", "page_index", "page_label",
                       "table_title", "row_position", "col_position", "n_pages",
                       "has_text_layer"}


def sha(p: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with p.open("rb") as fh:
        for c in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(c)
    return h.hexdigest()


def strip_volatile(obj):
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {k: strip_volatile(v) for k, v in obj.items()

def assign_eras(files) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Give the tree the era histogram the config asks for.

    A folder's era is only a hint about the files in it. Real drives hold files
    that were copied into an old folder last month and files that have not been
    opened since they were downloaded, so the mix of *modification* dates does
    not follow the folder layout exactly. Each file keeps its folder's era while
    that era still has room; the overflow -- almost all of it from the
    co-author stratum, which owns the most folders -- goes to whichever era is
    still short, nearest first.
    """
    n = len(files)
    quota = {e: int(round(v["weight"] * n)) for e, v in ERAS.items()}
    order = ["phd", "coauthor", "ra", "agent"]
    # let the scarce strata claim their own files first
    claim_order = sorted(order, key=lambda e: quota[e])
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    leftovers = []
    for era in claim_order:
        for f in sorted((f for f in files if f["era"] == era), key=lambda f: f["path"]):
            if quota[era] > 0:
                out[f["path"]] = era
                quota[era] -= 1
            else:
                leftovers.append(f)
    for f in sorted(leftovers, key=lambda f: f["path"]):
        own = order.index(f["era"]) if f["era"] in order else 1
        cands = sorted((e for e in order if quota[e] > 0),
                       key=lambda e: (abs(order.index(e) - own), -quota[e]))
        era = cands[0] if cands else f["era"]
        out[f["path"]] = era
        quota[era] = max(0, quota.get(era, 0) - 1)
    return out


def file_time(rec, era=None) -> datetime:
    era = era or rec["era"]
    y0, y1 = ERAS[era]["years"]

"""timestamps.py -- Phase 7.

One pass over a finished tree, setting atime, mtime and (where Windows lets us)
creation time on every file and folder from the era model.

A tree where everything was modified on the same night is useless, so:
  * each file draws a date inside its era's year range
  * within a project, raw comes before clean comes before output
  * v1 comes before v2; a "superseded" or "old" subfolder is older than its parent
  * the agent-era layer clusters into a run of activity in Feb-Aug 2026
  * a folder's mtime is its newest child's, applied bottom-up after every file

Every assigned time is recorded in keys/mtimes.parquet.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import json
import os
import sys
from ctypes import wintypes
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "world"))
import world as W  # noqa: E402

CFG = yaml.safe_load((HERE / "config.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
KEYS = ROOT / "keys"
ERAS = CFG["eras"]
# Nothing may carry the build date. The window closes at the end of August 2026.
CEILING = datetime(2026, 8, 31, 23, 59, 0)
FLOOR = datetime(2011, 1, 3, 8, 0, 0)

STAGE_RANK = [
    (("/raw", "/raw/", "raw_", "01_data", "rawdata", "raw-data", "/sources", "/source"), 0),
    (("/clean", "/clean/", "/derived", "/intermediate", "/extraction", "02_code"), 1),
    (("/output", "/outputs", "/figures", "/tables", "/results", "04_output"), 2),
]
OLD_MARKERS = ("/superseded", "/old", "/archive", "/attic", "/purana", "/not used",
               "/archived", "/old drives", "/.old_backup")


def _stage(path_lower: str) -> float:
    rank = 1.0
    for markers, r in STAGE_RANK:
        if any(m in path_lower for m in markers):
            rank = float(r)
    return rank


def _version_bump(name_lower: str) -> float:
    for tok, bump in (("v1", 0.0), ("v2", 1.0), ("v3", 2.0), ("_v4", 3.0),
                      ("(2)", 1.0), ("(3)", 2.0), ("final", 1.5), ("revised", 1.8)):
        if tok in name_lower:
            return bump
    return 0.0


def file_time(rec) -> datetime:
    era = rec["era"]
    y0, y1 = ERAS[era]["years"]
    g = W.rng_for("mtime", rec["path"])
    pl = "/" + rec["path"].lower()
    nl = rec["name"].lower()

    if era == "agent":
        # a real burst of recent activity, plus a tail across 2024-2025
        if g.random() < 0.42:
            base = datetime(2026, 2, 1) + timedelta(days=float(g.integers(0, 210)))
        else:
            base = datetime(2024, 1, 15) + timedelta(days=float(g.integers(0, 720)))
    else:
        span_days = (datetime(y1, 12, 20) - datetime(y0, 1, 10)).days
        base = datetime(y0, 1, 10) + timedelta(days=float(g.integers(0, span_days)))

    base += timedelta(days=_stage(pl) * float(g.integers(21, 75)))
    base += timedelta(days=_version_bump(nl) * float(g.integers(9, 40)))
    if any(m in pl for m in OLD_MARKERS):
        base -= timedelta(days=float(g.integers(120, 480)))

    # a working day, working hours, and not the same minute twice
    base = base.replace(hour=int(g.integers(8, 23)), minute=int(g.integers(0, 60)),
                        second=int(g.integers(0, 60)), microsecond=0)
    if base.weekday() == 6 and g.random() < 0.8:
        base -= timedelta(days=1)
    if base > CEILING:
        base = CEILING - timedelta(days=float(g.integers(1, 400)))
    if base < FLOOR:
        base = FLOOR + timedelta(days=float(g.integers(1, 200)))
    return base


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Windows creation time
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
_kernel32 = None
if os.name == "nt":
    try:
        _kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
        _kernel32.CreateFileW.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
        _kernel32.SetFileTime.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, ctypes.c_void_p,
                                          ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p]
    except Exception:                                        # pragma: no cover
        _kernel32 = None

GENERIC_WRITE = 0x40000000
FILE_SHARE = 0x00000007
OPEN_EXISTING = 3
FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS = 0x02000000
EPOCH_AS_FILETIME = 116444736000000000


class _FILETIME(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [("dwLowDateTime", wintypes.DWORD), ("dwHighDateTime", wintypes.DWORD)]


def _ft(dt: datetime) -> _FILETIME:
    ticks = int(dt.timestamp() * 10_000_000) + EPOCH_AS_FILETIME
    return _FILETIME(ticks & 0xFFFFFFFF, ticks >> 32)


def set_creation(path: Path, dt: datetime) -> bool:
    if _kernel32 is None:
        return False
    h = _kernel32.CreateFileW(str(path), GENERIC_WRITE, FILE_SHARE, None, OPEN_EXISTING,
                              FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS, None)
    if h in (None, -1, 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF):
        return False
    try:
        ft = _ft(dt)
        ok = _kernel32.SetFileTime(h, ctypes.byref(ft), ctypes.byref(ft), ctypes.byref(ft))
        return bool(ok)
    finally:
        _kernel32.CloseHandle(h)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def stamp_tree(root: Path, files, members=None):
    by_path = {f["path"]: f for f in files}
    rows, newest = [], {}
    ctime_ok = ctime_fail = 0
    paths = sorted(members) if members is not None else sorted(by_path)
    for rel in paths:
        rec = by_path.get(rel)
        p = root / rel
        if rec is None or not p.exists():
            continue
        dt = file_time(rec)
        ts = dt.timestamp()
        try:
            os.utime(p, (ts, ts))
        except OSError:
            continue
        if set_creation(p, dt):
            ctime_ok += 1
        else:
            ctime_fail += 1
        rows.append({"path": rel, "era": rec["era"], "role": rec["role"], "fmt": rec["fmt"],
                     "mtime_iso": dt.isoformat(), "mtime_epoch": ts})
        cur = p.parent
        while True:
            key = str(cur)
            if newest.get(key, 0) < ts:
                newest[key] = ts
            if cur == root:
                break
            cur = cur.parent

    # folders last, deepest first, so a parent sees its children's final times
    alldirs = sorted((d for d in root.rglob("*") if d.is_dir()),
                     key=lambda d: len(d.parts), reverse=True)
    for d in alldirs:
        ts = newest.get(str(d))
        if ts is None:
            g = W.rng_for("dirtime", str(d.relative_to(root)).replace("\\", "/"))
            dt = FLOOR + timedelta(days=float(g.integers(200, 5300)))
            ts = min(dt, CEILING).timestamp()
        try:
            os.utime(d, (ts, ts))
            set_creation(d, datetime.fromtimestamp(ts))
        except OSError:
            pass
        parent = d.parent
        if newest.get(str(parent), 0) < ts and parent != d:
            newest[str(parent)] = ts
    try:
        os.utime(root, (max(newest.values()), max(newest.values())))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        pass
    return rows, ctime_ok, ctime_fail


def main():
    man = json.loads((KEYS / "skeleton_manifest.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    files = man["files"]
    membership = json.loads((KEYS / "rung_membership.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    allrows = []
    for rung in CFG["ladder"]:
        root = ROOT / f"corpus_{rung}"
        if not root.exists():
            print(f"corpus_{rung}: not present, skipped")
            continue
        rows, ok, fail = stamp_tree(root, files, membership.get(str(rung)))
        for r in rows:
            r["rung"] = rung
        allrows += rows
        print(f"corpus_{rung}: {len(rows)} files stamped, creation-time set on {ok}, "
              f"unavailable on {fail}")
    try:
        import pandas as pd
        pd.DataFrame(allrows).to_parquet(KEYS / "mtimes.parquet", index=False)
        print(f"wrote keys/mtimes.parquet ({len(allrows)} rows)")
    except Exception as exc:
        (KEYS / "mtimes.json").write_text(json.dumps(allrows), encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"parquet unavailable ({exc}); wrote keys/mtimes.json instead")

    from collections import Counter
    top = [r for r in allrows if r["rung"] == CFG["ladder"][-1]]
    hist = Counter(r["mtime_iso"][:4] for r in top)
    print("year histogram (top rung):", dict(sorted(hist.items())))
    print("era shares:", {k: round(v / max(1, len(top)), 3)
                          for k, v in Counter(r["era"] for r in top).items()})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1	"""verify.py -- Phase 9.
2	
3	Thirteen checks. Every one prints PASS or FAIL with numbers. The build is not
4	finished until they all pass.
5	
6	    python verify.py                # everything
7	    python verify.py 3 4 7          # only those checks
8	    python verify.py --quick        # skip the slow full-corpus scans
9	"""
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import hashlib
13	import json
14	import os
15	import re
16	import sys
17	import time
18	import zipfile
19	from collections import Counter, defaultdict
20	from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
21	from datetime import datetime
22	from pathlib import Path
23	
24	import yaml
25	
26	HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
27	ROOT = HERE.parent
28	sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "world"))
29	
30	CFG = yaml.safe_load((HERE / "config.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
31	KEYS = ROOT / "keys"
32	LADDER = CFG["ladder"]
33	TOP = LADDER[-1]
34	MIX = CFG["format_mix"]
35	ERAS = CFG["eras"]
36	BUILD_DATE = datetime.now().date()
37	
38	BANNED = ["canary", "answer", "distractor", "synthetic", "generated", "harness",
39	          "ground truth", "seed", "test corpus", "filler"]
40	BANNED_RE = re.compile("|".join(re.escape(b) for b in BANNED), re.IGNORECASE)
41	TEXT_EXT = {".md", ".txt", ".csv", ".json", ".do", ".r", ".log", ".tex", ".py", ".xml", ".html"}
42	
43	RESULTS: list[tuple[str, bool, str]] = []
44	
45	
46	def report(name, ok, detail=""):
47	    RESULTS.append((name, ok, detail))
48	    print(f"[{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name}")
49	    for line in str(detail).splitlines():
50	        if line.strip():
51	            print(f"        {line}")
52	    return ok
53	
54	
55	def corpus(rung):
56	    return ROOT / f"corpus_{rung}"
57	
58	
59	def load_manifest():
60	    return json.loads((KEYS / "skeleton_manifest.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
61	
62	
63	def load_key():
64	    return json.loads((KEYS / "answer_key.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
65	
66	
67	def load_membership():
68	    p = KEYS / "rung_membership.json"
69	    return json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if p.exists() else {}
70	
71	
72	def bucket(fmt):
73	    if fmt in ("pdf", "csv", "md"):
74	        return fmt
75	    if fmt == "json":
76	        return "json_agent"
77	    return "tail"
78	
79	
80	def walk_files(root: Path):
81	    for p in root.rglob("*"):
82	        if p.is_file():
83	            yield p
84	
85	
86	# ==========================================================================
87	# 1. file counts per rung
88	# ==========================================================================
89	def check_1():
90	    lines, ok = [], True
91	    for rung in LADDER:
92	        root = corpus(rung)
93	        if not root.exists():
94	            lines.append(f"corpus_{rung}: MISSING")
95	            ok = False
96	            continue
97	        n = sum(1 for _ in walk_files(root))
98	        dev = (n - rung) / rung
99	        good = abs(dev) <= 0.03
100	        ok &= good
101	        lines.append(f"corpus_{rung}: {n} files, {dev:+.2%} vs target "
102	                     f"({'within' if good else 'OUTSIDE'} 3%)")
103	    return report("1. file counts per rung within 3% of ladder", ok, "\n".join(lines))
104	
105	
106	# ==========================================================================
107	# 2. format mix per rung
108	# ==========================================================================
109	def check_2():
110	    lines, ok = [], True
111	    for rung in LADDER:
112	        root = corpus(rung)
113	        if not root.exists():
114	            continue
115	        c = Counter()
116	        n = 0
117	        for p in walk_files(root):
118	            ext = p.suffix.lower().lstrip(".")
119	            c[bucket("json" if ext == "json" else ext)] += 1
120	            n += 1
121	        for b, want in MIX.items():
122	            got = c[b] / n if n else 0
123	            good = abs(got - want) <= 0.03
124	            ok &= good
125	            lines.append(f"corpus_{rung} {b:10s} {got:6.2%} vs {want:.2%} "
126	                         f"({got - want:+.3f}){'' if good else '  OUTSIDE'}")
127	    return report("2. format mix per rung within 3 points of config", ok, "\n".join(lines))
128	
129	
130	# ==========================================================================
131	# 3. fat PDF share and page ranges
132	# ==========================================================================
133	def _pagecount(args):
134	    path, = args
135	    try:
136	        from pypdf import PdfReader
137	        return path, len(PdfReader(path).pages)
138	    except Exception as exc:
139	        return path, -1
140	
141	
142	def check_3(quick=False):
143	    man = load_manifest()
144	    files = {f["path"]: f for f in man["files"]}
145	    root = corpus(TOP)
146	    lo, hi = CFG["fat_pdf_pages"]
147	    nlo, nhi = CFG["normal_pdf_pages"]
148	
149	    fat_expected, normal_expected = [], []
150	    for rel, f in files.items():
151	        if f["fmt"] != "pdf":
152	            continue
153	        spec = f["spec"]
154	        src = files.get(spec.get("source_path", "")) if spec.get("kind") == "duplicate" else None
155	        eff = src["spec"] if src else spec
156	        (fat_expected if eff.get("fat") else normal_expected).append(rel)
157	
158	    n_pdf = len(fat_expected) + len(normal_expected)
159	    share = len(fat_expected) / n_pdf if n_pdf else 0
160	    want = CFG["fat_pdf_share_of_pdfs"]
161	    lines = [f"pdfs {n_pdf}, fat {len(fat_expected)} = {share:.2%} (config {want:.2%})"]
162	    ok = abs(share - want) <= 0.02
163	
164	    sample = fat_expected if not quick else sorted(fat_expected)[:120]
165	    paths = [str(root / r) for r in sample if (root / r).exists()]
166	    bad, unread, counts = [], [], []
167	    if paths:
168	        with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=12) as ex:
169	            for path, n in ex.map(_pagecount, [(p,) for p in paths], chunksize=8):
170	                if n < 0:
171	                    unread.append(path)
172	                else:
173	                    counts.append(n)
174	                    if n < 200 or n > hi:
175	                        bad.append((Path(path).name, n))
176	    if counts:
177	        lines.append(f"fat page counts checked with pypdf on {len(counts)} files: "
178	                     f"min {min(counts)}, max {max(counts)}, mean {sum(counts)/len(counts):.0f}")
179	    if bad:
180	        ok = False
181	        lines.append(f"{len(bad)} fat documents outside 200-{hi} pages, e.g. {bad[:5]}")
182	    if unread:
183	        ok = False
184	        lines.append(f"{len(unread)} fat documents could not be read by pypdf")
185	    if quick:
186	        lines.append("(quick mode: page counts sampled, not exhaustive)")
187	    return report("3. fat-PDF share and page ranges", ok, "\n".join(lines))
188	
189	
190	# ==========================================================================
191	# 4. every evidence address resolves
192	# ==========================================================================

"""build_report.py -- Phase 10.

Assembles BUILD_REPORT.md from the artefacts the build left behind: the config,
the plan, the key, the rung report, the timestamp record, the format-mix
measurement of the real workspace, the phase timings and the verification
output. The prose sections -- judgment calls, fallbacks, and what a tester
needs to know -- are held here so the report is reproducible rather than
retyped.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
KEYS = ROOT / "keys"
LOGS = ROOT / "logs"
CFG = yaml.safe_load((HERE / "config.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
LADDER = CFG["ladder"]
TOP = LADDER[-1]


def jload(p, default=None):
    p = Path(p)
    if not p.exists():
        return default
    try:
        return json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return default


def human(n):
    for unit in ("B", "KB", "MB", "GB", "TB"):
        if n < 1024:
            return f"{n:.1f} {unit}"
        n /= 1024
    return f"{n:.1f} PB"


def tree_stats(root: Path):
    if not root.exists():
        return None
    n = size = 0
    ext = Counter()
    depths = []
    for p in root.rglob("*"):
        if p.is_file():
            n += 1
            try:
                size += p.stat().st_size
            except OSError:
                pass
            ext[p.suffix.lower().lstrip(".")] += 1
            depths.append(len(p.relative_to(root).parts))
    dirs = sum(1 for p in root.rglob("*") if p.is_dir())
    return {"files": n, "dirs": dirs, "bytes": size, "ext": ext,
            "max_depth": max(depths) if depths else 0}


def table(rows, header):
    out = ["| " + " | ".join(header) + " |",
           "|" + "|".join(["---"] * len(header)) + "|"]
    for r in rows:
        out.append("| " + " | ".join(str(x) for x in r) + " |")
    return "\n".join(out)


def main():
    man = jload(KEYS / "skeleton_manifest.json", {"files": [], "dirs": []})
    key = jload(KEYS / "answer_key.json", {})
    rung_report = jload(KEYS / "rung_report.json", [])
    mixes = jload(LOGS / "raship_format_mix.json", {})
    verify = jload(LOGS / "verify_last.json", [])
    timings = jload(LOGS / "phase_timings.json", {})
    slots = jload(KEYS / "canary_slots.json", {})
    files = man["files"]

    L = []
    A = L.append
    A("# Build report")
    A("")
    A(f"Built {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')} local time on Windows 11, "
      f"Python 3.11.5, from seed `{CFG['seed']}`.")
    A("")
    A(f"Output root `{CFG['output_root']}`. Four rungs at "
      f"`corpus_500`, `corpus_2000`, `corpus_5000`, `corpus_15000`; the key is outside "
      f"the trees at `keys/`. Nothing under the workspace copy at "
      f"`{CFG['raship_copy']}` was written to at any point.")
    A("")

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- config
    A("## 1. Configuration used")
    A("")
    A("```yaml")
    A((HERE / "config.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8").rstrip())
    A("```")
    A("")
    A("One field was changed from the brief's default: `raship_copy`. The brief gave "
      "`C:/Users/ali/Desktop/ra-ship` and told me to locate the copy rather than guess. "
      "There is no `ra-ship` at the Desktop root; the workspace is at "
      "`C:/Users/ali/Desktop/Projects/Code/ra-ship`, and that is what the config points at. "
      "Nothing else was changed.")
    A("")

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- world
    reg = jload(ROOT / "world" / "series_registry.json", {})
    vin = jload(ROOT / "world" / "series_vintages.json", [])
    brk = jload(ROOT / "world" / "series_breaks.json", [])
    cat = jload(ROOT / "world" / "document_catalogue.json", [])
    A("## 2. The world")
    A("")
    A(table([
        ["Series in the registry", len(reg)],
        ["Vintages", len(vin)],
        ["Recorded breaks", len(brk)],
        ["- rebasings", sum(1 for b in brk if b["break_type"] == "rebasing")],
        ["- unit switches", sum(1 for b in brk if b["break_type"] == "unit_switch")],
        ["- row-label drifts", sum(1 for b in brk if b["break_type"] == "row_label_drift")],
        ["Documents implied by the world", len(cat)],
        ["- of those, in the fat tier", sum(1 for d in cat if d["fat"])],
        ["Table placements those documents carry", sum(len(d["embeds"]) for d in cat)],
    ], ["", "count"]))
    A("")
    A("Fiscal years FY2010-11 to FY2025-26. Every value is drawn from a macro backbone "
      "(real growth, inflation, population, nominal GDP, the exchange rate) so the fiscal, "
      "provincial, external, social and sector series move together and carry the pandemic "
      "dip and the FY2022-23 inflation spike. No published figure is reproduced.")
    A("")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ plan
    A("## 3. Counts per rung")
    A("")
    rows = []
    for rung in LADDER:
        st = tree_stats(ROOT / f"corpus_{rung}")
        if st is None:
            rows.append([f"corpus_{rung}", "NOT BUILT", "", "", "", ""])
            continue
        rows.append([f"corpus_{rung}", st["files"], st["dirs"], human(st["bytes"]),
                     st["max_depth"],
                     f"{(st['files'] - rung) / rung:+.2%}"])
    A(table(rows, ["rung", "files", "folders", "size", "max file depth", "vs target"]))
    A("")
    if rung_report:
        A("Derivation of the smaller rungs:")
        A("")
        rows = [[r["target"], r.get("selected"), r.get("protected", "-"),
                 r.get("distractors", "-"), r.get("copied", "-"), r.get("missing", "-")]
                for r in rung_report]
        A(table(rows, ["rung", "selected", "held fixed", "shadow files", "copied", "missing"]))
        A("")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- format mix
    A("## 4. Format mix, against the real workspace")
    A("")
    if mixes:
        rows = []
        for b in ["pdf", "csv", "md", "json_agent", "tail"]:
            cfgv = CFG["format_mix"][b]
            real = mixes["bucket_shares"].get(b, 0)
            rows.append([b, f"{cfgv:.2%}", f"{real:.2%}", f"{real - cfgv:+.3f}"])
        rows.append(["other (png, ts, js, py, ...)", "-",
                     f"{mixes['bucket_shares'].get('other', 0):.2%}", "-"])
        A(table(rows, ["bucket", "config", "real workspace", "gap"]))
        A("")
        A(f"Measured over {mixes['total_files']} files in the workspace copy, excluding "
          f"`02_tool_runs/`, virtualenvs and `.git`, as the brief specifies. "
          f"**The config was not changed from this measurement** -- that is Ali's call. "
          f"The gaps worth knowing about:")
        A("")
        A("- The real workspace is 52.6% PDF against a configured 66%. The configured mix "
          "is the more punishing one, which is the right direction for a measurement, but a "
          "baseline taken here will overstate how PDF-dominated a real drive is.")
        A("- The real workspace is 2.6% Markdown against a configured 11%. The corpus has "
          "roughly four times the note density of the original. If the point is to measure "
          "how badly stale notes mislead retrieval, that is a deliberate over-weighting; if "
          "the point is to mirror the drive, this is the largest single gap.")
        A("- 23.8% of the real workspace is in buckets the config does not model at all: "
          "images (574 `.png`, 39 `.jpg`), source code (171 `.ts`, 135 `.js`, 111 `.py`) and "
          "194 extensionless files. The corpus has none of these. A retrieval layer that "
          "trips over screenshots or a `node_modules` tree will not be caught here.")
        A("")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- key
    qs = key.get("questions", [])
    A("## 5. The key")
    A("")
    A(table([[t, c] for t, c in sorted(Counter(q["type"] for q in qs).items())] +
            [["**total**", len(qs)]], ["question type", "count"]))
    A("")
    A(table([
        ["Evidence-bearing files", len(key.get("answer_files", {}))],
        ["Shadow files placed", len(key.get("distractor_files", {}))],
        ["Shadow files per question (top rung)",
         f"{sum(len(q['must_not_cite']) for q in qs) / max(1, len(qs)):.1f} mean"],
        ["Copy clusters recorded", len(key.get("scattered_duplicate_clusters", []))],
        ["Files whose name lies about their contents", len(key.get("misnamed_files", []))],
        ["Authored note anchors", len(key.get("sediment_anchors", []))],
        ["Cross-file links", len(key.get("relationship_links", []))],
        ["Damaged files", len(key.get("unreadable_files", []))],
        ["Archives", len(key.get("archives", []))],
    ], ["", "count"]))
    A("")
    fin = key.get("finalised", {})
    if fin:
        A(f"Address resolution: {fin.get('addresses')} evidence addresses, "
          f"{fin.get('resolved_pages')} resolved to a page index and printed page label from "
          f"the document sidecars, {fin.get('hashed')} files hashed.")
        A("")

    # -------------------------------------------------------------- timings
    if timings:
        A("## 6. Run time by phase")
        A("")
        A(table([[k, f"{v:.0f}s" if isinstance(v, (int, float)) else v]
                 for k, v in timings.items()], ["phase", "elapsed"]))
        A("")

    # --------------------------------------------------------------- slots
    if slots:
        A("## 7. Marker slots")
        A("")
        A(f"`keys/canary_slots.json` holds {slots.get('count')} recommended placements. "
          f"Nothing was planted. `generator/plant_canaries.py` takes a CSV of phrase, path "
          f"and page, backs up each original, injects, and restores the original timestamps "
          f"so planting leaves no trace in the mtime distribution; "
          f"`--restore` puts everything back.")
        A("")
        A(table([[s["path"], s["format"], s["depth"], s["era"],
                  s.get("page_index", "-")] for s in slots.get("slots", [])],
                ["path", "format", "depth", "era", "page"]))
        A("")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ verification
    A("## 8. Verification")
    A("")
    if verify:
        rows = [[v["check"], "PASS" if v["pass"] else "**FAIL**"] for v in verify]
        A(table(rows, ["check", "result"]))
        A("")
        A("Full output:")
        A("")
        A("```")
        for v in verify:
            A(f"[{'PASS' if v['pass'] else 'FAIL'}] {v['check']}")
            for line in str(v["detail"]).splitlines():
                if line.strip():
                    A(f"        {line}")
        A("```")
    else:
        A("`logs/verify_last.json` was not present when this report was assembled.")
    A("")

    A((HERE / "report_prose.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
      if (HERE / "report_prose.md").exists() else "")

    (ROOT / "BUILD_REPORT.md").write_text("\n".join(L) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote BUILD_REPORT.md ({sum(len(x) for x in L)} chars)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## 9. Judgment calls

Every decision below was made without being able to ask. Each says what the brief left
open, what I chose, and why.

**1. The registry has more than sixty series.** The brief asks for "~60 series" and then
lists the coverage it wants. Six jurisdictions times six provincial measures is thirty-six
series on its own; adding the national accounts, fiscal, monetary, external, social and
sector families brings the total to 86. Coverage was treated as the requirement and the
count as the estimate.

**2. `fat` means "in the fat tier", not "a long publication type".** The catalogue's PSDP
volumes and provincial white papers draw 100-200 and 100-250 pages, which straddles the
200-page floor the config sets for the fat tier. Verification check 3 requires every fat
document to be at least 200 pages, so a catalogue document is marked fat only when its page
draw actually reaches 200. The fat *share* is then held at the configured 18% by raising
passive documents into the tier, never by cutting the share.

**3. Where the vocabulary ban is enforced.** The brief bans a list of words "anywhere in the
tree" and simultaneously mandates the paths `harness/seed_docs/`, `harness/keys/canary_slots.json`
and `harness/generator/plant_canaries.py`, which contain three of the banned words. The ban
is therefore enforced over the corpus trees, which is what a reader would ever open; the
tooling and key directories outside them are exempt. Verification check 7 scans
`corpus_15000` only.

**4. One phrase in the paper-title vocabulary had to be replaced.** "A Synthetic Control
Approach" is a real method name and was in the generator's list of paper-title qualifiers,
which put a banned word into document titles, filenames and extraction outputs. It was
replaced at source with "A Regression Discontinuity Approach" and everything downstream was
rebuilt. The alternative -- laundering the string after the fact -- would have broken
reproducibility.

**5. The smaller rungs nest their shadow files rather than holding them fixed.** The brief
asks for the answers, shadows, notes and agent layer to be identical at every rung, and
separately for 100-150 questions with 10-20 shadows each. Those two requirements cannot both
hold: the shadow set alone is a floor of roughly 1,900 files, and the 500 and 2,000 rungs
cannot contain it. Each question keeps its first *k* shadows, where *k* is 1 at the 500 rung,
4 at 2,000, 10 at 5,000 and all of them at 15,000, and the set at each rung is a strict
subset of the one above. Evidence files, the authored note anchors, the misnamed files and
the copy clusters are held identical at every rung, so every question is answerable at every
rung with the same evidence; only the density of things that shadow it changes. The key
records rung membership in `keys/rung_membership.json` so a scorer knows which shadows were
present when a question was asked.

**6. Era strata are a property of the file, not only of the folder.** Assigning every file
the era of its folder produced a modification-date histogram half made of the co-author
stratum, because that stratum owns the most folders. The timestamp pass therefore assigns
eras to hit the configured weights exactly: a file keeps its folder's era while that era has
quota, and the overflow goes to the nearest era that is still short. 79.5% of files keep
their folder's era. The result is a drive where an old project folder contains a handful of
files touched recently and a recent folder contains a few things copied in from years ago,
which is what a real drive looks like.

**7. The modification-date ceiling is 31 August 2026.** Verification requires that no file
carries the build date. The agent era runs to 2026, so the window is closed at the end of
August rather than at the build date itself, which leaves the recent layer clustered in
February-August 2026 as the brief asks.

**8. Sub-document addresses are resolved after the documents are built, from the documents'
own sidecars.** The brief forbids searching the corpus to find where things went. Page
indices cannot be known before layout, so Phase 3 records the logical address -- document,
chapter, table ordinal, series vintage, fiscal year -- at placement time, and
`finalize_key.py` joins those to the page index, printed page label and table title that the
PDF factory wrote into `keys/pdf_index/` for its own output. That is the factory reporting
its placement, not a search.

**9. Copies and damaged files come out of the file budget, not on top of it.** Six per cent
duplicates and 0.4% unreadable files are realised by converting planned passive files into
copies and damaged files rather than by adding new ones, so the rung totals stay on target.

**10. The absence probes are phrased as document titles and notification numbers.** An
absence question needs a string that provably does not occur. Series-and-year absences are
hard to prove absent because the number itself may appear coincidentally, so the probes are
full document titles for publications that were never obtained and notification numbers that
are not in the entity list. Verification check 6 greps every text file, PDF text layer and
archive member for them.

## 10. Fallbacks taken

- None on dependencies: `numpy`, `pandas`, `pyarrow`, `reportlab`, `pypdf`, `python-docx`,
  `openpyxl`, `pillow` and `pyyaml` all installed cleanly, so neither the DOCX fallback nor
  the plain-PDF fallback was needed.
- Creation time is set through `SetFileTime` in `kernel32` via `ctypes`, since `os.utime`
  only reaches access and modification times on Windows. Where that call fails the file
  still gets correct access and modification times and the failure is counted in the
  timestamp log.
- Passive Stata and R scripts are self-contained: they embed their data rather than reading a
  sibling file. This was the data factory's call, made so that every passive script would
  actually run. It is a realism gap -- a real drive's do-files read files -- and it means
  verification check 13 has only the five deliberately linked scripts to resolve. The five
  scripts the key depends on do reference real inputs, and one of them deliberately points at
  a path that no longer exists.

## 11. What a tester needs to know before running a baseline

The corpus is not a pile of documents with some right answers hidden in it. Every number in
every table comes from one registry of economic series, and each series exists in two to five
*vintages* -- successive publications that revise earlier years, sometimes rebase the levels
from one base year to another, sometimes switch from Rs billion to Rs million, and almost
always change the row label they are printed under. That means two documents can give
different numbers for the same series and year and both be correct, and it means the label a
question uses may not be the label the correct document prints. `keys/series_breaks.json`
records every break; `keys/answer_key.json` records, for each question, the vintage the
expected value comes from, which other vintages are acceptable with a caveat, and which files
must not be cited and why. Score against the vintage, not against a bare number.

Three consequences for a baseline run. First, the shadow files are built to beat the correct
file on lexical match: they keep the plain obvious row label and the obvious document title
while the correct document has drifted, so a retrieval layer that ranks by surface similarity
will prefer them, and that is the measurement. Second, roughly one file in six is a copy of
another somewhere unrelated in the tree, with nothing marking which is canonical, and 0.4%
of files are genuinely broken -- truncated, encrypted, image-only, a zero-byte CSV, a Stata
file with a bad header -- so a pipeline that treats an unreadable file as an empty one will
silently lose evidence. Third, the fifteen absence questions have no answer in the corpus at
all; a system that produces a confident number for them is failing in the way that matters
most, and they are the cheapest signal in the set.

Run the ladder in order and compare the same questions across rungs. The rungs are strict
subsets of one another and every question is answerable at every rung with identical
evidence at identical paths, so any change in the result between `corpus_500` and
`corpus_15000` is degradation from corpus size and shadow density, not from a different task.
The nesting means shadow density rises with the rung as well as file count; if you need to
separate those two effects, `keys/rung_membership.json` tells you exactly which shadow files
were present at each rung.

Finally: nothing has been planted. `keys/canary_slots.json` recommends twenty placements and
`generator/plant_canaries.py` performs the injection, backing up originals and restoring
timestamps. One recommended slot is a scan with no text layer, and it is expected to fail
without optical character recognition -- that failure is the point of the slot, not a defect
in the build.

"""resolve_citations.py -- fallback for the memo citations.

The three authored research memos cite tables by page. Those citations are
written as `{{CITE:<doc_id>:<series_id>}}` tokens and can only be resolved once
the PDF factory has written the sidecar for the cited document.

The sediment factory resolves them as part of its own run. This is the backstop:
it writes any sediment record that is still missing, and rewrites any file in
the corpus that still carries a token. Running it when there is nothing to do is
a no-op.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent
KEYS = ROOT / "keys"
INDEX = KEYS / "pdf_index"
CORPUS = ROOT / "corpus_15000"
SEEDS = ROOT / "seed_docs"
TOKEN = re.compile(r"\{\{CITE:([^:}]+):([^}]+)\}\}")


def load_index():
    """series_id -> list of (doc_id, title, page_index, page_label, table_title, path)."""
    by_doc, by_series = {}, {}
    for f in INDEX.glob("*.json"):
        try:
            sc = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if not sc.get("has_text_layer", True):
            continue
        for t in sc.get("tables", []):
            rec = (sc.get("doc_id"), sc["path"], t.get("page_index"), t.get("page_label"),
                   t.get("table_title"))
            by_doc.setdefault((sc.get("doc_id"), t.get("series_id")), []).append(rec)
            by_series.setdefault(t.get("series_id"), []).append(rec)
    return by_doc, by_series


def title_for(rel_path: str, catalogue) -> str:
    name = Path(rel_path).stem
    for d in catalogue:
        if d["filename"].rsplit(".", 1)[0] == name:
            return d["title"]
    return name


def render(doc_title, page_index, page_label, table_title):
    return (f"{doc_title} (p. {page_index + 1} of the file, printed page {page_label}), "
            f"{table_title}")


def resolve_text(text, by_doc, by_series, catalogue, log):
    def sub(m):
        doc_id, sid = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        hits = by_doc.get((doc_id, sid)) or by_series.get(sid)
        if not hits:
            log.append(f"  UNRESOLVED {doc_id}:{sid}")
            return "the table cited in the accompanying document"
        hits = sorted(hits, key=lambda r: (r[0] != doc_id, r[2]))
        _did, path, pi, pl, tt = hits[0]
        out = render(title_for(path, catalogue), pi, pl, tt)
        log.append(f"  {doc_id}:{sid} -> {out}")
        return out
    return TOKEN.sub(sub, text)


def main():
    catalogue = json.loads((ROOT / "world" / "document_catalogue.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    by_doc, by_series = load_index()
    if not by_doc:
        print("no sidecars present; nothing can be resolved yet")
        return 1
    work = json.loads((KEYS / "work" / "sediment.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    seed_man = {m["id"]: m for m in
                json.loads((SEEDS / "manifest.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))}
    log, wrote, fixed = [], 0, 0

    for rec in work:
        spec = rec.get("spec", {})
        if spec.get("kind") != "authored":
            continue
        out = CORPUS / rec["path"]
        src_id = spec.get("source_id")
        if not out.exists():
            m = seed_man.get(src_id)
            if not m:
                continue
            text = (SEEDS / m["source_file"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            log.append(f"WRITE {rec['path']}")
            text = resolve_text(text, by_doc, by_series, catalogue, log)
            out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            out.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
            wrote += 1
        else:
            text = out.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
            if TOKEN.search(text):
                log.append(f"FIX {rec['path']}")
                out.write_text(resolve_text(text, by_doc, by_series, catalogue, log),
                               encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
                fixed += 1

    # anything anywhere in the tree that still carries a token
    stragglers = 0
    for p in CORPUS.rglob("*.md"):
        text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        if TOKEN.search(text):
            log.append(f"FIX {p.relative_to(CORPUS)}")
            p.write_text(resolve_text(text, by_doc, by_series, catalogue, log),
                         encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
            stragglers += 1

    (ROOT / "logs" / "resolve_citations.log").write_text("\n".join(log), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"written {wrote}, rewritten {fixed}, stragglers {stragglers}")
    print(f"unresolved tokens: {sum(1 for x in log if 'UNRESOLVED' in x)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""reconcile.py -- make the corpus match the plan exactly.

Deletes anything the plan does not name (orphans left by a rename, and the
empty stubs Windows leaves behind when a filename containing a colon is written
through an alternate data stream), then reports what each factory still owes.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import json, sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
C = ROOT / "corpus_15000"
KEYS = ROOT / "keys"


def main(prune=True):
    man = json.loads((KEYS / "skeleton_manifest.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    files = man["files"]
    planned = {f["path"] for f in files}
    planned_lower = {p.lower() for p in planned}
    removed = 0
    if prune:
        for p in sorted(C.rglob("*")):
            if not p.is_file():
                continue
            rel = p.relative_to(C).as_posix()
            if rel.lower() not in planned_lower:
                try:
                    p.unlink(); removed += 1
                except OSError as e:
                    print("  could not remove", rel, e)
    missing = [f for f in files if not (C / f["path"]).exists()]
    visible = sum(1 for p in C.rglob("*") if p.is_file())
    print(f"pruned            : {removed}")
    print(f"visible on disk   : {visible}")
    print(f"planned           : {len(planned)}")
    print(f"still owed        : {len(missing)}")
    print(f"  by owner        : {dict(Counter(f['owner'] for f in missing))}")
    print(f"  by fmt          : {dict(Counter(f['fmt'] for f in missing))}")
    (ROOT / "logs" / "reconcile.json").write_text(
        json.dumps({"pruned": removed, "visible": visible, "missing":
                    [f["path"] for f in missing]}, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    return missing


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(prune="--no-prune" not in sys.argv)

## 9. Judgment calls

Every decision below was made without being able to ask. Each says what the brief left
open, what I chose, and why.

**1. The registry has more than sixty series.** The brief asks for "~60 series" and then
lists the coverage it wants. Six jurisdictions times six provincial measures is thirty-six
series on its own; adding the national accounts, fiscal, monetary, external, social and
sector families brings the total to 86. Coverage was treated as the requirement and the
count as the estimate.

**2. `fat` means "in the fat tier", not "a long publication type".** The catalogue's PSDP
volumes and provincial white papers draw 100-200 and 100-250 pages, which straddles the
200-page floor the config sets for the fat tier. Verification check 3 requires every fat
document to be at least 200 pages, so a catalogue document is marked fat only when its page
draw actually reaches 200. The fat *share* is then held at the configured 18% by raising
passive documents into the tier, never by cutting the share.

**3. Where the vocabulary ban is enforced.** The brief bans a list of words "anywhere in the
tree" and simultaneously mandates the paths `harness/seed_docs/`, `harness/keys/canary_slots.json`
and `harness/generator/plant_canaries.py`, which contain three of the banned words. The ban
is therefore enforced over the corpus trees, which is what a reader would ever open; the
tooling and key directories outside them are exempt. Verification check 7 scans
`corpus_15000` only.

**4. One phrase in the paper-title vocabulary had to be replaced.** "A Synthetic Control
Approach" is a real method name and was in the generator's list of paper-title qualifiers,
which put a banned word into document titles, filenames and extraction outputs. It was
replaced at source with "A Regression Discontinuity Approach" and everything downstream was
rebuilt. The alternative -- laundering the string after the fact -- would have broken
reproducibility.

**5. The smaller rungs nest their shadow files rather than holding them fixed.** The brief
asks for the answers, shadows, notes and agent layer to be identical at every rung, and
separately for 100-150 questions with 10-20 shadows each. Those two requirements cannot both
hold: the shadow set alone is a floor of roughly 1,900 files, and the 500 and 2,000 rungs
cannot contain it. Each question keeps its first *k* shadows, where *k* is 1 at the 500 rung,
4 at 2,000, 10 at 5,000 and all of them at 15,000, and the set at each rung is a strict
subset of the one above. Evidence files, the authored note anchors, the misnamed files and
the copy clusters are held identical at every rung, so every question is answerable at every
rung with the same evidence; only the density of things that shadow it changes. The key
records rung membership in `keys/rung_membership.json` so a scorer knows which shadows were
present when a question was asked.

**6. Era strata are a property of the file, not only of the folder.** Assigning every file
the era of its folder produced a modification-date histogram half made of the co-author
stratum, because that stratum owns the most folders. The timestamp pass therefore assigns
eras to hit the configured weights exactly: a file keeps its folder's era while that era has
quota, and the overflow goes to the nearest era that is still short. 79.5% of files keep
their folder's era. The result is a drive where an old project folder contains a handful of
files touched recently and a recent folder contains a few things copied in from years ago,
which is what a real drive looks like.

**7. The modification-date ceiling is 31 August 2026.** Verification requires that no file
carries the build date. The agent era runs to 2026, so the window is closed at the end of
August rather than at the build date itself, which leaves the recent layer clustered in
February-August 2026 as the brief asks.

**8. Sub-document addresses are resolved after the documents are built, from the documents'
own sidecars.** The brief forbids searching the corpus to find where things went. Page
indices cannot be known before layout, so Phase 3 records the logical address -- document,
chapter, table ordinal, series vintage, fiscal year -- at placement time, and
`finalize_key.py` joins those to the page index, printed page label and table title that the
PDF factory wrote into `keys/pdf_index/` for its own output. That is the factory reporting
its placement, not a search.

**9. Copies and damaged files come out of the file budget, not on top of it.** Six per cent
duplicates and 0.4% unreadable files are realised by converting planned passive files into
copies and damaged files rather than by adding new ones, so the rung totals stay on target.

**10. The absence probes are phrased as document titles and notification numbers.** An
absence question needs a string that provably does not occur. Series-and-year absences are
hard to prove absent because the number itself may appear coincidentally, so the probes are
full document titles for publications that were never obtained and notification numbers that
are not in the entity list. Verification check 6 greps every text file, PDF text layer and
archive member for them.

## 10. Fallbacks taken

- None on dependencies: `numpy`, `pandas`, `pyarrow`, `reportlab`, `pypdf`, `python-docx`,
  `openpyxl`, `pillow` and `pyyaml` all installed cleanly, so neither the DOCX fallback nor
  the plain-PDF fallback was needed.
- Creation time is set through `SetFileTime` in `kernel32` via `ctypes`, since `os.utime`
  only reaches access and modification times on Windows. Where that call fails the file
  still gets correct access and modification times and the failure is counted in the
  timestamp log.
- Passive Stata and R scripts are self-contained: they embed their data rather than reading a
  sibling file. This was the data factory's call, made so that every passive script would
  actually run. It is a realism gap -- a real drive's do-files read files -- and it means
  verification check 13 has only the five deliberately linked scripts to resolve. The five
  scripts the key depends on do reference real inputs, and one of them deliberately points at
  a path that no longer exists.

## 11. What a tester needs to know before running a baseline

The corpus is not a pile of documents with some right answers hidden in it. Every number in
every table comes from one registry of economic series, and each series exists in two to five
*vintages* -- successive publications that revise earlier years, sometimes rebase the levels
from one base year to another, sometimes switch from Rs billion to Rs million, and almost
always change the row label they are printed under. That means two documents can give
different numbers for the same series and year and both be correct, and it means the label a
question uses may not be the label the correct document prints. `keys/series_breaks.json`
records every break; `keys/answer_key.json` records, for each question, the vintage the
expected value comes from, which other vintages are acceptable with a caveat, and which files
must not be cited and why. Score against the vintage, not against a bare number.

Three consequences for a baseline run. First, the shadow files are built to beat the correct
file on lexical match: they keep the plain obvious row label and the obvious document title
while the correct document has drifted, so a retrieval layer that ranks by surface similarity
will prefer them, and that is the measurement. Second, roughly one file in six is a copy of
another somewhere unrelated in the tree, with nothing marking which is canonical, and 0.4%
of files are genuinely broken -- truncated, encrypted, image-only, a zero-byte CSV, a Stata
file with a bad header -- so a pipeline that treats an unreadable file as an empty one will
silently lose evidence. Third, the fifteen absence questions have no answer in the corpus at
all; a system that produces a confident number for them is failing in the way that matters
most, and they are the cheapest signal in the set.

Run the ladder in order and compare the same questions across rungs. The rungs are strict
subsets of one another and every question is answerable at every rung with identical
evidence at identical paths, so any change in the result between `corpus_500` and
`corpus_15000` is degradation from corpus size and shadow density, not from a different task.
The nesting means shadow density rises with the rung as well as file count; if you need to
separate those two effects, `keys/rung_membership.json` tells you exactly which shadow files
were present at each rung.

Finally: nothing has been planted. `keys/canary_slots.json` recommends twenty placements and
`generator/plant_canaries.py` performs the injection, backing up originals and restoring
timestamps. One recommended slot is a scan with no text layer, and it is expected to fail
without optical character recognition -- that failure is the point of the slot, not a defect
in the build.

Update: I noticed (via my monitor) that pdf_factory.py got re-invoked twice, concurrently, against a regenerated pdf.json (9233 records now, down from my original 9234 — presumably the title fix). Both concurrent runs completed cleanly: DONE 9233/9233, 0 errors each. I did not start these runs.

I verified the result rather than assuming it was fine, because of one real risk with my resumability design: it skips a file whenever its sidecar+PDF already exist on disk, without re-checking whether the current spec still matches what's on disk. So if the "title fix" changed a title at a path that was already built in my original 9234-file run, that file would have been silently skipped and would still carry the OLD title.

Checked this directly: sampled 200 random records from the current pdf.json, opened the actual on-disk PDF's cover page via pypdf, and compared to spec['title'] verbatim — 176 checked (excluding scanned), 0 mismatches. Also confirmed 0 missing files against the current 9233-record list, and total corpus size is now 3.67 GB (up slightly from 3.66 GB). One minor loose end: 9240 sidecar files exist on disk vs 9233 current records — 7 are orphans left over from whichever path(s) dropped out of the work list between the 9234- and 9233-record versions. I left those alone (didn't delete anything) since the contract doesn't ask for sidecar cleanup and removing files felt like the wrong default without being asked.

Also flagging for awareness: running two full 12-worker invocations of the same factory concurrently (24 workers on this 16-core box) works but is wasteful and carries a real Windows file-write race risk (two processes opening the same output path for write at once) — it happened to complete without errors this time, but I wouldn't rely on that. If pdf.json needs another fix in the future, either delete the affected files'/sidecars' before rerunning, or run the factory only once at a time.

No action needed from me right now — corpus looks consistent and correct as of this second run.
</agent-message>

        kind = spec.get("kind")

        if scanned:
